question: Which aspect of the financial system do the Basel Norms focus on?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Banking.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Basel Norms **are the norms issued by the **Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS)** f**or the international banking regulations.**
 
• The goal of these norms is to coordinate banking regulations around the world and strengthen the international banking system.
 
• BCBS consists of 27 representatives from countries across the globe including India.
 
• Presently the Basel Committee has issued 3 guidelines to realize its objective which are Basel I, II and III.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Basel l **

 
 
• These rules are introduced in the year **1988 **which focused originally on the credit risk faced by the banks.
 
• According to these guidelines, all the banks were necessary to maintain a capital adequacy ratio of 8% of the credit risk. 
 
 
 
• **Basel II**
 
 
• Basel II was introduced in the year **2004 **and aimed at more regulation than Basel I. India is currently following Basel II guidelines.

 It introduced three pillars upon which regulation is to be conducted by the banks:

 Minimum Capital Requirements, Supervisory Review Process, and Disclosure & Market Discipline.
 
 
 
• **Basel III**
 
 
• It was introduced in **2010**.
 
• Its objective was to make a resilient and transparent banking system, improve banking sector shock-absorbing capacity and more focus on Capital Adequacy Ratio.
 
• Basel III has created 2 liquidity ratios which are Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) i.e. to have a high-quality liquid asset to meet short-term requirements (30 days) and Net Stable Funds Rate (NSFR) requires banks to maintain a stable funding profile to meet medium-term requirements (1 year).
 
• The three pillars of Basel III norms were Enhanced Minimum Capital Requirements, Enhanced Supervisory Review Process and Enhanced Disclosure & Market Discipline.
 
• India has introduced Basel III norms in March 2019 but RBI extended the deadline to March 2020 and in light of the COVID-19 pandemic it was further extended by 6 months.
